title: Low End Theory at 35
hook: 35 years ago this month, Low End Theory dropped.
voiceover: 35 years ago this month, Low End Theory dropped. September 24, 1991, A Tribe Called Quest, Jive Records. Everyone posts the green and red cover. Here's the part the pages skip. On Verses from the Abstract, that upright bass is not a sample. It's Ron Carter, the jazz bassist who played with Miles Davis, in the studio, playing live. Carter has said he agreed on 1 condition, no profanity on his track, and Q-Tip kept his word. The rest of the album is jazz records cut by a DJ's ear, Minnie Riperton under Check the Rhime, Art Blakey under Excursions. A rap album that treated jazz like a crate, not a costume. Where were you when this dropped?
caption: The Low End Theory, A Tribe Called Quest, Jive, September 24, 1991. 35 years. The detail that matters: Ron Carter, who played bass with Miles Davis, played live on Verses from the Abstract and, by his own account, asked for no profanity on his track. Elsewhere it's Minnie Riperton under Check the Rhime and Art Blakey under Excursions. Where were you when this dropped?
